title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 71-72
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 71 to 72 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'ब्रह्मण्यो ब्रह्मकृद्ब्रह्मा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविवर्धनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 71 to 72 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 71 to 72.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 71 to 72** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **ब्रह्मण्यो ब्रह्मकृद्ब्रह्मा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविवर्धनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**ब्रह्मण्यो ब्रह्मकृद्ब्रह्मा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविवर्धनः । ब्रह्मविद्ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मी ब्रह्मज्ञो ब्राह्मणप्रियः ॥** **महाक्रमो महाकर्मा महातेजा महोरगः । महाक्रतुर्महायज्वा महायज्ञो महाहविः ॥**

He is kind to the learned, the maker of Brahma and Brahma himself. The Supreme Brahman who nurtures sacred knowledge is that God of gods. Knower of Brahman, the true Brahmin, wise in the Self, dear to the Brahmins. Of great strides, great deeds, great radiance and the great serpent is he. The great rite, the great sacrificer, the great sacrifice and the great offering is that God of gods.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 71 to 72 mean?
faq.a: He is kind to the learned, the maker of Brahma and Brahma himself. The Supreme Brahman who nurtures sacred knowledge is that God of gods. Knower of Brahman, the true Brahmin, wise in the Self, dear to the Brahmins. Of great strides, great deeds, great radiance and the great serpent is he. The great rite, the great sacrificer, the great sacrifice and the great offering is that God of gods.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
